claim: The emitted relay telemetry can exercise byte-volume correlation and timing correlation at one-second or coarser resolution.
rationale: The transferability note explicitly preserves these two uses despite the integer-second eventtime limit; the builder correlates inbound and outbound bytes.

claim: A passing geovelocity test with this technique demonstrates that the production rule correctly performs live GeoIP and ASN enrichment of login source addresses.
rationale: The catalog explicitly says synthetic country tags on documentation-range IPs do not exercise the live GeoIP/ASN enrichment on which the production rule depends.

claim: An evaluation of this technique against a production SIEM measured 98 percent recall and a false-positive rate below 1 percent.
rationale: The catalog describes synthetic distributions and limitations, not a measured production-SIEM recall or false-positive result.

claim: An inbound IPS alert followed by accepted inbound traffic and later egress establishes an observable progression hypothesis, rather than proof of compromise.
rationale: The catalog explicitly limits this ordered, role-aware victim correlation to an observable progression hypothesis.

claim: The generated DNS records include WHOIS registration-age metadata, allowing this technique to exercise the cited detector's registration-age scoring.
rationale: The transferability note says the emitted domains carry no registration metadata and Replicant performs no WHOIS lookup, so registration-age scoring is not exercised.

claim: This technique emits a benign NXDOMAIN trickle that can be isolated as the negative control stream.
rationale: The entry declares emits_foil true and describes the generated benign NXDOMAIN trickle; the builder appends that foil.

claim: The parser-visible event timestamps preserve each chosen relay lag exactly in milliseconds, so a 20 ms inbound-to-outbound delta can be validated directly.
rationale: EventRecord.eventtime is integer seconds and relay lag is dithered to whole seconds; the transferability note explicitly excludes sub-second delta detection.

claim: This technique has received formal ArcSight certification for its emitted CEF records.
rationale: Neither the catalog nor the generator code supplies evidence of formal certification. A policy forbidding certification claims would not by itself prove the historical factual negation.

claim: With the supplied synthetic country tags, the emitted login sequence can exercise distance and threshold logic even though real source-IP enrichment is outside its coverage.
rationale: The transferability note makes exactly this distinction between supplied-tag threshold logic and live enrichment.

claim: Because this entry describes a normal consistent-country user in benign_baseline, selecting controls=negative yields a generated normal-login foil for it.
rationale: The entry has no emits_foil flag, which defaults to false. Its builder emits only the anomalous login sequence, and negative controls therefore yield no events; benign_baseline prose alone does not declare a shipped foil.

claim: The technique can exercise organization-wide first-contact novelty by introducing domains that were not queried by any host during its baseline phase.
rationale: The baseline and novel distributions, transferability note, and distinct generated domain sets explicitly support organization-wide novelty.

claim: The generated relay byte-volume distribution has been empirically matched to captures from a live Check Point appliance with less than 2 percent statistical error.
rationale: The catalog and code specify synthetic correlated byte generation but supply no live-appliance distribution study or measured statistical error.

claim: Since the generated labels sit under .invalid, a green result still exercises the realistic-effective-TLD and domain-registration-enrichment stages of a DGA detector.
rationale: The catalog explicitly says reserved .invalid labels do not exercise those stages, although lexical features and NXDOMAIN clustering transfer.

claim: Production evaluation found this technique improves detection recall by 25 percentage points over REP-008.
rationale: The source distinguishes organization-wide novelty from per-host novelty, but gives no comparative production recall measurements.

claim: When a detector matches the ordered IPS-to-egress pattern, those records prove that an exploit executed successfully and the victim was compromised.
rationale: The transferability note expressly denies proof of exploit execution or compromise from this observable pattern.

claim: Although its .invalid domains do not cover reputation or registration enrichment, this technique can exercise qname lexical features and NXDOMAIN-clustering logic.
rationale: These are precisely the covered signals retained in the parser-only transferability note.
